issues.description: Method addGuestStudents: the problem statement (task description and UML) and the solution implement a single-parameter method addGuestStudents(int), but the template declares addGuestStudents with two parameters (int, boolean). Specifically, problem_statement.md instructs/depicts addGuestStudents(int), solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java defines public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents), while template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java defines public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput). This parameter mismatch (extra boolean in the template) will cause compilation/test failures and confuses students because they will implement/expect the single-parameter API described in the exercise and used by tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template's public API to match the problem statement and solution. Change the template method signature to: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) { /* TODO */ }. If input validation is desired, perform it inside this single-parameter method or implement a private/helper overload; do not expose a boolean parameter in the public signature so that the template matches the specification and tests.

issues.description: The concept is "adding guest students". The problem statement specifies a public method addGuestStudents(int). The solution implements public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents). The template declares public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput) — i.e. the same method name but with an extra boolean parameter. This parameter-arity mismatch between the template and both the problem description and the solution will confuse students: they cannot directly implement or use the API the statement describes, and automated tests or example usages that expect addGuestStudents(int) will not match the template's signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template's public method declaration to match the problem statement and solution: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents). If input validation behavior is desired, implement validation inside that method or add a private helper/overload, but keep the public API signature consistent with the assignment and solution.
